+"""Global runtime parameters.

+

+Secret: which global parameters exist, which environment variable enables

+strict arguments mode, and which argv positions may supply global

+parameters in each mode.

+"""

+

+from . import messages as _messages

+from .errors import CliError

+from .synopsis import Synopsis

+

+_STRICT_ENV = "APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"

+_GLOBALS = Synopsis(

+    "[--path=<path>] [--url=<url>] [--user=<id>] [--[no-]color] "

+    "[--debug[=<group>]] [--quiet]"

+)

+

+

+class RuntimeConfig:

+    """Read-only view of the global runtime configuration."""

+

+    def __init__(self, values, strict):

+        self._values = dict(values)

+        self._strict = strict

+

+    def path(self):

+        return self._values.get("path")

+

+    def url(self):

+        return self._values.get("url")

+

+    def user(self):

+        return self._values.get("user")

+

+    def color(self):

+        return self._values.get("color", True)

+

+    def debug(self):

+        return bool(self._values.get("debug", False))

+

+    def quiet(self):

+        return bool(self._values.get("quiet", False))

+

+    def strict(self):

+        return self._strict

+

+    def as_dict(self):

+        return {

+            "path": self.path(),

+            "url": self.url(),

+            "user": self.user(),

+            "color": self.color(),

+            "debug": self.debug(),

+            "quiet": self.quiet(),

+            "strict_args_mode": self.strict(),

+        }

+

+

+def extract(items, env):

+    """Split global parameters out of ``items``.

+

+    Returns ``(RuntimeConfig, remaining_tokens)``. In strict mode only tokens

+    before the first positional word are considered global.

+    """

+    strict = bool(env.get(_STRICT_ENV, ""))

+    values = {}

+    remaining = []

+    seen_positional = False

+    for token in items:

+        if not token.is_option():

+            seen_positional = True

+            remaining.append(token)

+            continue

+        if strict and seen_positional:

+            remaining.append(token)

+            continue

+        key, value, status = _GLOBALS.interpret(token.name, token.value)

+        if status == Synopsis.UNKNOWN:

+            remaining.append(token)

+        elif status == Synopsis.OK:

+            values[key] = value

+        else:

+            raise CliError(_messages.global_parameter_error(

+                key, needs_value=(status == Synopsis.NEEDS_VALUE)))

+    return RuntimeConfig(values, strict), remaining

+"""Lexical syntax of the command line.

+

+Secret: how raw argv strings are split into option tokens (``--key=value``,

+``--flag``) and positional words, including the ``--`` terminator.

+"""

+

+

+class Token:

+    """One lexical unit of the command line."""

+

+    __slots__ = ("_text", "_name", "_value", "_option")

+

+    def __init__(self, text, name=None, value=None, option=False):

+        self._text = text

+        self._name = name

+        self._value = value

+        self._option = option

+

+    def is_option(self):

+        return self._option

+

+    @property

+    def text(self):

+        """The token exactly as the user typed it."""

+        return self._text

+

+    @property

+    def name(self):

+        """Option name without leading dashes (``None`` for positionals)."""

+        return self._name

+

+    @property

+    def value(self):

+        """Option value as a string, or ``None`` when no ``=`` was given."""

+        return self._value

+

+    def __repr__(self):

+        return f"Token({self._text!r})"

+

+

+def positional(text):

+    """Build a positional word token."""

+    return Token(text)

+

+

+def lex(argv):

+    """Split raw argv strings into tokens."""

+    result = []

+    options_ended = False

+    for raw in argv:

+        if options_ended:

+            result.append(positional(raw))

+        elif raw == "--":

+            options_ended = True

+        elif raw.startswith("--") and len(raw) > 2:

+            body = raw[2:]

+            if "=" in body:

+                name, value = body.split("=", 1)

+            else:

+                name, value = body, None

+            result.append(Token(raw, name, value, option=True))

+        else:

+            result.append(positional(raw))

+    return result

+"""Record rendering.

+

+Secret: how a list of records is rendered in each supported output format.

+"""

+

+import csv

+import io

+import json

+

+_FORMATS = ("table", "json", "csv", "yaml", "ids", "count")

+

+

+def supported_formats():

+    return list(_FORMATS)

+

+

+def _table(records, fields):

+    rows = [[str(r.get(f, "")) for f in fields] for r in records]

+    widths = [max([len(f)] + [len(row[i]) for row in rows])

+              for i, f in enumerate(fields)]

+    lines = ["  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(fields, widths)).rstrip()]

+    lines += ["  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(row, widths)).rstrip()

+              for row in rows]

+    return "\n".join(lines)

+

+

+def _csv(records, fields):

+    buffer = io.StringIO()

+    writer = csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator="\n")

+    writer.writerow(fields)

+    for record in records:

+        writer.writerow([record.get(f, "") for f in fields])

+    return buffer.getvalue().rstrip("\n")

+

+

+def _yaml(records, fields):

+    lines = ["---"]

+    for record in records:

+        for index, field in enumerate(fields):

+            lead = "- " if index == 0 else "  "

+            lines.append(f"{lead}{field}: {json.dumps(record.get(field, ''))}")

+    return "\n".join(lines)

+

+

+def render(records, fields, fmt):

+    """Render ``records`` (dicts) restricted to ``fields`` in format ``fmt``.

+

+    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unsupported format.

+    """

+    fields = list(fields)

+    if fmt == "table":

+        return _table(records, fields)

+    if fmt == "json":

+        return json.dumps([{f: r.get(f) for f in fields} for r in records])

+    if fmt == "csv":

+        return _csv(records, fields)

+    if fmt == "yaml":

+        return _yaml(records, fields)

+    if fmt == "ids":

+        return " ".join(str(r.get(fields[0], "")) for r in records)

+    if fmt == "count":

+        return str(len(records))

+    raise ValueError(fmt)

+

+

+_MAPPING_FORMATS = ("list", "json", "yaml")

+

+

+def supported_mapping_formats():

+    return list(_MAPPING_FORMATS)

+

+

+def render_mapping(mapping, fmt):

+    """Render a single key/value mapping. Raises ``ValueError`` for an

+    unsupported format."""

+    if fmt == "list":

+        width = max((len(k) for k in mapping), default=0)

+        return "\n".join(f"{k.ljust(width)}  {v}" for k, v in mapping.items())

+    if fmt == "json":

+        return json.dumps(mapping)

+    if fmt == "yaml":

+        return "\n".join(["---"] + [f"{k}: {json.dumps(v)}" for k, v in mapping.items()])

+    raise ValueError(fmt)

+"""Command storage.

+

+Secret: how commands are stored as a tree, how names and aliases are

+matched, and how children are ordered for display.

+"""

+

+from .synopsis import Synopsis

+

+

+def _sort_key(name):

+    return (name.casefold(), name)

+

+

+class CommandNode:

+    """One command (or the root) in the command tree."""

+

+    def __init__(self, name, parent=None):

+        self._name = name

+        self._parent = parent

+        self._children = {}

+        self._aliases = {}

+        self._handler = None

+        self._synopsis_text = ""

+        self._synopsis = Synopsis("")

+        self._description = ""

+        self._alias = None

+        self._defaults = {}

+

+    def _configure(self, handler, synopsis, description, alias, defaults):

+        self._handler = handler

+        self._synopsis_text = synopsis or ""

+        self._synopsis = Synopsis(self._synopsis_text)

+        self._description = description or ""

+        self._alias = alias

+        self._defaults = dict(defaults or {})

+

+    @property

+    def name(self):

+        return self._name

+

+    @property

+    def path(self):

+        """Full space-separated command path ('' for the root)."""

+        words = []

+        node = self

+        while node._parent is not None:

+            words.append(node._name)

+            node = node._parent

+        return " ".join(reversed(words))

+

+    @property

+    def parent(self):

+        return self._parent

+

+    @property

+    def description(self):

+        return self._description

+

+    @property

+    def alias(self):

+        return self._alias

+

+    @property

+    def synopsis(self):

+        return self._synopsis

+

+    def defaults(self):

+        return dict(self._defaults)

+

+    def is_root(self):

+        return self._parent is None

+

+    def is_runnable(self):

+        return self._handler is not None

+

+    def has_children(self):

+        return bool(self._children)

+

+    def children(self):

+        return [self._children[n] for n in sorted(self._children, key=_sort_key)]

+

+    def child_names(self):

+        return sorted(self._children, key=_sort_key)

+

+    def find_child(self, word):

+        """Match ``word`` against child names, then child aliases."""

+        if word in self._children:

+            return self._children[word]

+        canonical = self._aliases.get(word)

+        return self._children.get(canonical) if canonical else None

+

+    def run(self, context):

+        return self._handler(context)

+

+    def _child(self, name, create):

+        if name not in self._children and create:

+            if name in self._aliases:

+                raise ValueError(f"'{name}' is already an alias under '{self.path}'")

+            self._children[name] = CommandNode(name, self)

+        return self._children.get(name)

+

+    def _add_alias(self, alias, canonical):

+        if alias in self._children or self._aliases.get(alias, canonical) != canonical:

+            raise ValueError(f"alias '{alias}' conflicts under '{self.path}'")

+        self._aliases[alias] = canonical

+

+

+class CommandTree:

+    """Registry of all commands."""

+

+    def __init__(self):

+        self._root = CommandNode("")

+

+    @property

+    def root(self):

+        return self._root

+

+    def register(self, path, handler=None, *, synopsis="", description="",

+                 alias=None, defaults=None):

+        """Register (or update) the command at space-separated ``path``.

+

+        Missing parent commands are created as non-runnable groups.

+        """

+        words = path.split()

+        if not words:

+            raise ValueError("command path must not be empty")

+        node = self._root

+        for word in words:

+            node = node._child(word, create=True)

+        node._configure(handler, synopsis, description, alias, defaults)

+        if alias:

+            node.parent._add_alias(alias, node.name)

+        return node

+

+    def find(self, words):

+        """Return the node at exactly ``words`` (aliases allowed) or ``None``."""

+        node = self._root

+        for word in words:

+            node = node.find_child(word)

+            if node is None:

+                return None

+        return None if node is self._root else node

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+# appctl — design by information hiding

+

+Each entry below is a design decision that is hard to make or likely to

+change. Each one lives in exactly one module (under `appctl_core/`), and that

+module's *secret* is the decision. Other modules depend only on the module's

+interface, which stays valid if the secret changes. No module hands its

+internal data structures to another: interfaces exchange strings, numbers,

+plain lists/dicts built fresh for the caller, or opaque objects with methods.

+

+| # | Decision (likely to change) | Module | Secret (one sentence) | Interface |

+|---|-----------------------------|--------|-----------------------|-----------|

+| 1 | Lexical syntax of a command line | `tokens.py` | How raw argv strings are split into option tokens (`--k=v`, `--flag`) and positional words, including the `--` terminator. | `lex(argv)`, `positional(text)`, `Token.is_option() / .name / .value / .text` |

+| 2 | Convenience argv rewrites | `rewrites.py` | Which shortcut spellings (`<cmd> --help`, `--version`) are rewritten into canonical commands, and how. | `apply(tokens) -> tokens` |

+| 3 | Global runtime parameters and strict mode | `runtime_config.py` | Which global parameters exist, which env var turns on strict mode, and which argv positions may supply globals. | `extract(tokens, env) -> (RuntimeConfig, tokens)`; `RuntimeConfig` getters |

+| 4 | Synopsis grammar | `synopsis.py` | The textual grammar of synopsis strings and how each part is classified (positional, keyed, flag, negatable flag, generic, malformed, optional, repeating). | `Synopsis(text)` query methods + `interpret(name, value)` |

+| 5 | Validation policy and default application | `binding.py` | The order in which argument checks run, which conditions are errors, how errors are batched, and when defaults are filled in. | `bind(path, synopsis, defaults, words, options) -> BoundArguments`; raises `MissingPositional` / `CliError` |

+| 6 | Similarity algorithm for suggestions | `suggest.py` | The distance metric, threshold and tie-breaking that pick a single deterministic "Did you mean" candidate. | `suggest(target, candidates) -> str or None` |

+| 7 | Curated synonym table | `synonyms.py` | Which common command-name variants map to which canonical names. | `synonym_for(word) -> str or None` |

+| 8 | Command storage, alias lookup and ordering | `command_tree.py` | How commands are stored as a tree, how names and aliases are matched, and how children are ordered. | `CommandTree.register/find/root`, `CommandNode` query methods |

+| 9 | Command resolution algorithm | `dispatch.py` | How positional words are walked down the tree and when leftover words become arguments rather than unknown subcommands. | `resolve(tree, words) -> (node, remaining_words)` |

+| 10 | User-facing message wording | `messages.py` | The exact text of every error/notice and the program's display name. | One function per message |

+| 11 | Help and usage layout | `help_text.py` | How help listings, command help pages and usage lines are laid out (ordering, column alignment, sections). | `top_level_help`, `command_help`, `usage_line`, `composite_usage` |

+| 12 | Output streams and prefixes | `output.py` | Which stream each kind of output goes to, its prefix, and how `--quiet` / `--debug` affect it. | `Output.error/warning/success/log/line/usage/debug` |

+| 13 | Record rendering formats | `formatter.py` | How lists of records are rendered as table/json/csv/yaml/ids/count. | `render(records, fields, fmt) -> str`, `supported_formats()` |

+| 14 | Which commands exist and what they do | `catalog.py` | The set of built-in commands, their synopses, aliases, defaults, descriptions and handler behavior. | `register_all(tree)` |

+| 15 | Wiring of the pipeline | `app.py` | The order the stages run in (lex → rewrite → globals → resolve → bind → run) and how failures map to exit codes. | `run(argv, env, stdout, stderr) -> int` |

+

+`errors.py` holds the shared exception types (`CliError`, `MissingPositional`)

+that make up part of several interfaces. It has no secret of its own.

+

+`appctl.py` is the executable entry point and just calls `app.run`.

+"""Built-in command catalog.

+

+Secret: which commands exist, together with their synopses, aliases,

+defaults, descriptions and what each handler does.

+"""

+

+from . import dispatch, formatter, help_text

+from .errors import CliError

+

+VERSION = "1.0.0"

+

+_SITES = [

+    {"name": "main", "type": "standard", "title": "Main Site", "status": "active"},

+    {"name": "blog", "type": "blog", "title": "Company Blog", "status": "active"},

+    {"name": "shop", "type": "store", "title": "Shop", "status": "archived"},

+]

+_PLUGINS = [

+    {"name": "akismet", "status": "active", "version": "5.3"},

+    {"name": "hello-dolly", "status": "inactive", "version": "1.7.2"},

+]

+_USERS = [

+    {"ID": 1, "user_login": "admin", "user_email": "admin@example.com", "roles": "administrator"},

+    {"ID": 2, "user_login": "editor", "user_email": "editor@example.com", "roles": "editor"},

+]

+_POSTS = [

+    {"ID": 1, "post_title": "Hello world!", "post_status": "publish", "post_type": "post"},

+    {"ID": 2, "post_title": "Sample Page", "post_status": "publish", "post_type": "page"},

+]

+_OPTIONS = {"blogname": "My Site", "siteurl": "https://example.com", "admin_email": "admin@example.com"}

+_CONFIG = {"DB_NAME": "app", "DB_HOST": "localhost", "DEBUG": "false"}

+

+

+# --- shared helpers -------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _render(ctx, records, default_fields):

+    args = ctx.args

+    field = args.option("field")

+    fields = [field] if field else (

+        args.option("fields").split(",") if args.option("fields") else default_fields)

+    fmt = args.option("format", "table")

+    if field and fmt == "table":

+        for record in records:

+            ctx.out.line(str(record.get(field, "")))

+        return 0

+    try:

+        ctx.out.line(formatter.render(records, fields, fmt))

+    except ValueError:

+        raise CliError(f"Invalid format: {fmt}. Supported formats: "

+                       + ", ".join(formatter.supported_formats()))

+    return 0

+

+

+def _each(ctx, verb, noun):

+    items = ctx.args.positionals

+    for item in items:

+        ctx.out.log(f"{verb} {noun} '{item}'.")

+    ctx.out.success(f"{verb} {len(items)} of {len(items)} {noun}s.")

+    return 0

+

+

+def _filtered(records, key, value):

+    return [r for r in records if value is None or str(r.get(key)) == str(value)]

+

+

+def _require_targets_or_all(ctx, noun):

+    if not ctx.args.positionals and not ctx.args.option("all"):

+        raise CliError(f"Please specify one or more {noun}s, or use --all.")

+    if ctx.args.option("all"):

+        return [p["name"] for p in _PLUGINS]

+    return ctx.args.positionals

+

+

+# --- cache ----------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _cache_set(verb):

+    def handler(ctx):

+        key, value, group, expiration = ctx.args.positionals[:4]

+        ctx.out.success(f"{verb} object '{key}' in group '{group}' "

+                        f"(expires: {expiration}): {value}")

+        return 0

+    return handler

+

+

+def _cache_step(sign):

+    def handler(ctx):

+        key, offset, group = ctx.args.positionals[:3]

+        try:

+            amount = int(offset)

+        except ValueError:

+            raise CliError(f"Offset must be an integer, got '{offset}'.")

+        ctx.out.line(str(sign * amount))

+        ctx.out.log(f"Adjusted '{key}' in group '{group}' by {sign * amount}.")

+        return 0

+    return handler

+

+

+def _cache_get(ctx):

+    key, group = ctx.args.positionals[:2]

+    raise CliError(f"Object with key '{key}' and group '{group}' not found.")

+

+

+def _cache_delete(ctx):

+    key, group = ctx.args.positionals[:2]

+    ctx.out.success(f"Object '{key}' deleted from group '{group}'.")

+    return 0

+

+

+def _cache_flush(ctx):

+    ctx.out.success("The cache was flushed.")

+    return 0

+

+

+# --- cli ------------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _cli_version(ctx):

+    ctx.out.line(f"appctl {VERSION}")

+    return 0

+

+

+def _cli_info(ctx):

+    info = dict(ctx.config.as_dict(), version=VERSION)

+    fmt = ctx.args.option("format")

+    try:

+        ctx.out.line(formatter.render_mapping(info, fmt))

+    except ValueError:

+        raise CliError(f"Invalid format: {fmt}. Supported formats: "

+                       + ", ".join(formatter.supported_mapping_formats()))

+    return 0

+

+

+def _cli_has_command(ctx):

+    words = " ".join(ctx.args.positionals).split()

+    return 0 if ctx.tree.find(words) is not None else 1

+

+

+# --- config ---------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _config_get(ctx):

+    name = ctx.args.positional(0)

+    if name not in _CONFIG:

+        raise CliError(f"The constant or variable '{name}' is not defined in the config file.")

+    ctx.out.line(_CONFIG[name])

+    return 0

+

+

+def _config_set(ctx):

+    name, value = ctx.args.positionals[:2]

+    return 0

+

+

+def _config_delete(ctx):

+    name = ctx.args.positional(0)

+    if name not in _CONFIG:

+

+

+def _config_list(ctx):

+    filters = ctx.args.positionals

+    strict = ctx.args.option("strict")

+    records = [{"name": k, "value": v} for k, v in _CONFIG.items()

+    return _render(ctx, records, ["name", "value"])

+

+

+# --- help -----------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _help(ctx):

+    words = ctx.args.positionals

+    if not words:

+        ctx.out.usage(help_text.top_level_help(ctx.tree))

+        return 0

+    node, _ = dispatch.resolve(ctx.tree, words)

+    ctx.out.usage(help_text.command_help(node))

+    return 0

+

+

+# --- option ---------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _option_get(ctx):

+    key = ctx.args.positional(0)

+    if key not in _OPTIONS:

+        raise CliError(f"Could not get '{key}' option. Does it exist?")

+    ctx.out.line(_OPTIONS[key])

+    return 0

+

+

+def _option_write(verb):

+    def handler(ctx):

+        key = ctx.args.positional(0)

+        value = ctx.args.positional(1)

+        if value is None:

+            raise CliError("Please provide a value for the option.")

+        ctx.out.success(f"{verb} '{key}' option (autoload: {ctx.args.option('autoload')}).")

+        return 0

+    return handler

+

+

+def _option_list(ctx):

+    search = ctx.args.option("search")

+    exclude = ctx.args.option("exclude")

+    records = [{"option_name": k, "option_value": v} for k, v in _OPTIONS.items()

+    return _render(ctx, records, ["option_name", "option_value"])

+

+

+# --- plugin ---------------------------------------------------------------

+

+def _plugin_bulk(verb):

+        names = _require_targets_or_all(ctx, "plugin")

+            ctx.out.log(f"Plugin '{name}' {verb}.")

+        ctx.out.success(f"{verb.capitalize()} {len(names)} of {len(names)} plugins.")

+        return 0

+    return handler

+

+

+def _plugin_install(ctx):

+        ctx.out.log(f"Installing {name}{suffix}...")

+        if ctx.args.option("activate"):

+    return 0

+

+def _plugin_list(ctx):

+    return _render(ctx, records, ["name", "status", "version"])

+    return 0

+

+

+def _post_get(ctx):

+    return _render(ctx, records, list(records[0]))

+

+

+def _post_list(ctx):

+    records = list(_POSTS)

+    return _render(ctx, records, ["ID", "post_title", "post_status", "post_type"])

+

+

+def _update_fields(noun):

+    def handler(ctx):

+        fields = {k: v for k, v in ctx.args.options().items()

+                  if k not in ("skip-email",)}

+        if not fields:

+            raise CliError("Need some fields to update.")

+        changes = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(fields.items()))

+        for target in ctx.args.positionals:

+            ctx.out.success(f"Updated {noun} '{target}': {changes}.")

+        return 0

+

+# --- site -----------------------------------------------------------------

+def _site_create(ctx):

+def _site_empty(ctx):

+

+def _site_list(ctx):

+

+

+def _user_create(ctx):

+        return 0

+

+def _user_get(ctx):

+def _user_list(ctx):

+

+

+# --- registration ---------------------------------------------------------

+

+_LIST_FORMAT = "[--field=<field>] [--fields=<fields>] [--format=<format>]"

+def register_all(tree):

+"""Command resolution.

+

+Secret: how positional words are walked down the command tree, and when

+leftover words become arguments of the matched command rather than unknown

+subcommands.

+"""

+

+from . import messages as _messages

+from .errors import CliError

+from .suggest import suggest

+

+

+def resolve(tree, words):

+    """Find the deepest command matching the leading ``words``.

+

+    Returns ``(node, remaining_words)``. Raises ``CliError`` for an unknown

+    top-level command, or an unknown subcommand under a group that cannot

+    itself run.

+    """

+    node = tree.root

+    words = list(words)

+    consumed = 0

+    for word in words:

+        if not node.has_children():

+            break

+        child = node.find_child(word)

+        if child is None:

+            if node.is_runnable() and not node.is_root():

+                break

+            suggestion = suggest(word, node.child_names())

+            if node.is_root():

+                raise CliError(_messages.unregistered_command(word, suggestion))

+            raise CliError(_messages.unregistered_subcommand(

+                word, node.path, suggestion))

+        node = child

+        consumed += 1

+    return node, words[consumed:]

+"""Synopsis grammar.

+

+Secret: the textual grammar of synopsis strings and how each part is

+classified (positional, keyed parameter, flag, negatable flag, generic keyed

+field, malformed; optional and repeating modifiers).

+"""

+

+import re

+

+_NAME = r"[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*"

+_PLACEHOLDER = r"[\w|.-]+"

+

+_POSITIONAL = re.compile(rf"^<({_PLACEHOLDER})>$")

+_GENERIC = re.compile(rf"^--<({_PLACEHOLDER})>=<({_PLACEHOLDER})>$")

+_KEYED = re.compile(rf"^--({_NAME})=<({_PLACEHOLDER})>$")

+_KEYED_OPTIONAL_VALUE = re.compile(rf"^--({_NAME})\[=<({_PLACEHOLDER})>\]$")

+_FLAG = re.compile(rf"^--({_NAME})$")

+_NEGATABLE_FLAG = re.compile(rf"^--\[no-\]({_NAME})$")

+

+_POSITIONAL_KIND = "positional"

+_KEYED_KIND = "keyed"

+_FLAG_KIND = "flag"

+_GENERIC_KIND = "generic"

+_MALFORMED_KIND = "malformed"

+

+_REPEAT = "..."

+

+

+class _Part:

+    __slots__ = ("text", "kind", "name", "optional", "repeating", "value_optional")

+

+    def __init__(self, text, kind, name=None, optional=False, repeating=False,

+                 value_optional=False):

+        self.text = text

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.name = name

+        self.optional = optional

+        self.repeating = repeating

+        self.value_optional = value_optional

+

+

+def _outer_brackets(text):

+    """True when the leading '[' is closed by the trailing ']'."""

+    if not (text.startswith("[") and text.endswith("]")):

+        return False

+    depth = 0

+    for index, char in enumerate(text):

+        if char == "[":

+            depth += 1

+        elif char == "]":

+            depth -= 1

+            if depth == 0 and index != len(text) - 1:

+                return False

+    return depth == 0

+

+

+def _parse_part(text):

+    core = text

+    optional = repeating = False

+    if core.endswith(_REPEAT):

+        repeating, core = True, core[: -len(_REPEAT)]

+    if _outer_brackets(core):

+        optional, core = True, core[1:-1]

+        if core.endswith(_REPEAT):

+            repeating, core = True, core[: -len(_REPEAT)]

+

+    def part(kind, name=None, value_optional=False):

+        return _Part(text, kind, name, optional, repeating, value_optional)

+

+    match = _POSITIONAL.match(core)

+    if match:

+        return part(_POSITIONAL_KIND, match.group(1))

+    match = _GENERIC.match(core)

+    if match:

+        return part(_GENERIC_KIND, match.group(1))

+    match = _KEYED.match(core)

+    if match:

+        return part(_KEYED_KIND, match.group(1))

+    match = _KEYED_OPTIONAL_VALUE.match(core)

+    if match:

+        return part(_KEYED_KIND, match.group(1), value_optional=True)

+    match = _FLAG.match(core) or _NEGATABLE_FLAG.match(core)

+    if match:

+        return part(_FLAG_KIND, match.group(1))

+    return _Part(text, _MALFORMED_KIND)

+

+

+class Synopsis:

+    """A parsed synopsis that answers questions about accepted arguments."""

+

+    OK = "ok"

+    UNKNOWN = "unknown"

+    NEEDS_VALUE = "needs-value"

+    TAKES_NO_VALUE = "takes-no-value"

+

+    def __init__(self, text=""):

+        self._parts = [_parse_part(p) for p in (text or "").split()]

+        self._options = {}

+        for part in self._parts:

+            if part.kind in (_KEYED_KIND, _FLAG_KIND):

+                self._options[part.name] = part

+

+    def text(self):

+        return " ".join(part.text for part in self._parts)

+

+    def malformed_parts(self):

+        return [p.text for p in self._parts if p.kind == _MALFORMED_KIND]

+

+    def _positionals(self):

+        return [p for p in self._parts if p.kind == _POSITIONAL_KIND]

+

+    def required_positional_count(self):

+        return sum(1 for p in self._positionals() if not p.optional)

+

+    def positional_limit(self):

+        """Maximum number of positional words, or ``None`` if unbounded."""

+        positionals = self._positionals()

+        if any(p.repeating for p in positionals):

+            return None

+        return len(positionals)

+

+    def positional_names(self):

+        return [p.name for p in self._positionals()]

+

+    def option_names(self):

+        """Declared keyed-parameter and flag names, in declaration order."""

+        return list(self._options)

+

+    def required_option_names(self):

+        return [name for name, p in self._options.items() if not p.optional]

+

+    def accepts_any_option(self):

+        return any(p.kind == _GENERIC_KIND for p in self._parts)

+

+    def requires_generic_option(self):

+        """Name of a mandatory generic field placeholder, or ``None``."""

+        for p in self._parts:

+            if p.kind == _GENERIC_KIND and not p.optional:

+                return p.name

+        return None

+

+    def interpret(self, name, value):

+        """Interpret a supplied option.

+

+        ``value`` is the supplied string or ``None`` when no ``=`` was given.

+        Returns ``(key, value, status)`` where status is one of the class

+        constants. Flags yield booleans; keyed parameters yield strings.

+        """

+        part = self._options.get(name)

+        if part is not None:

+            if part.kind == _FLAG_KIND:

+                if value is None:

+                    return name, True, self.OK

+                return name, None, self.TAKES_NO_VALUE

+            if value is None and part.value_optional:

+                return name, True, self.OK

+            if value is None or value == "":

+                return name, None, self.NEEDS_VALUE

+            return name, value, self.OK

+        if name.startswith("no-") and value is None:

+            negated = self._options.get(name[3:])

+            if negated is not None and negated.kind == _FLAG_KIND:

+                return negated.name, False, self.OK

+        if self.accepts_any_option():

+            return name, (True if value is None else value), self.OK

+        return name, None, self.UNKNOWN

+"""Similarity-based suggestions.

+

+Secret: the distance metric (case-insensitive Levenshtein), the acceptance threshold, the

+tie-breaking order and the precedence of curated synonyms used to pick a

+single deterministic "Did you mean" candidate.

+"""

+

+from . import synonyms as _synonyms

+

+_THRESHOLD = 2

+

+

+def _distance(a, b):

+    previous = list(range(len(b) + 1))

+    for i, char_a in enumerate(a, 1):

+        current = [i]

+        for j, char_b in enumerate(b, 1):

+            current.append(min(

+                previous[j] + 1,

+                current[j - 1] + 1,

+                previous[j - 1] + (char_a != char_b),

+            ))

+        previous = current

+    return previous[-1]

+

+

+def suggest(target, candidates):

+    """Return the best candidate for a mistyped ``target``, or ``None``."""

+    pool = sorted(set(candidates), key=lambda c: (c.casefold(), c))

+    if not pool:

+        return None

+    synonym = _synonyms.synonym_for(target)

+    if synonym is not None and synonym in pool:

+        return synonym

+    folded = target.casefold()

+    best = min(pool, key=lambda c: _distance(folded, c.casefold()))

+    if best != target and _distance(folded, best.casefold()) <= _THRESHOLD:

+        return best

+    return None

+"""Argument validation and binding.

+

+Secret: the order in which argument checks run, which conditions count as

+errors, how associative-argument errors are batched, and when defaults are

+filled in.

+"""

+

+from . import messages as _messages

+from .errors import CliError, MissingPositional

+from .suggest import suggest

+from .synopsis import Synopsis

+

+

+class BoundArguments:

+    """Validated arguments with defaults applied."""

+

+    def __init__(self, positionals, options):

+        self._positionals = list(positionals)

+        self._options = dict(options)

+

+    @property

+    def positionals(self):

+        return list(self._positionals)

+

+    def positional(self, index, default=None):

+        if index < len(self._positionals):

+            return self._positionals[index]

+        return default

+

+    def option(self, name, default=None):

+        return self._options.get(name, default)

+

+    def has_option(self, name):

+        return name in self._options

+

+    def options(self):

+        return dict(self._options)

+

+

+def _check_positionals(synopsis, words):

+    if len(words) < synopsis.required_positional_count():

+        raise MissingPositional()

+    limit = synopsis.positional_limit()

+    if limit is not None and len(words) > limit:

+        raise CliError(_messages.too_many_positionals(words[limit:]))

+

+

+def _bind_options(synopsis, options):

+    bound = {}

+    needs_value, takes_no_value, unknown = [], [], []

+    for name, value in options:

+        key, interpreted, status = synopsis.interpret(name, value)

+        if status == Synopsis.OK:

+            bound[key] = interpreted

+        elif status == Synopsis.NEEDS_VALUE:

+            bound.pop(key, None)

+            needs_value.append(key)

+        elif status == Synopsis.TAKES_NO_VALUE:

+            takes_no_value.append(key)

+        elif name not in unknown:

+            unknown.append(name)

+

+    required = synopsis.required_option_names()

+    errors = [_messages.missing_parameter(key)

+              for key in required if key not in bound]

+    errors += [_messages.parameter_needs_value(key)

+               for key in dict.fromkeys(needs_value)

+               if key not in required and key not in bound]

+    errors += [_messages.parameter_takes_no_value(key)

+               for key in dict.fromkeys(takes_no_value)]

+    generic = synopsis.requires_generic_option()

+    if generic and not any(k not in synopsis.option_names() for k in bound):

+        errors.append(_messages.missing_parameter(generic))

+    known = synopsis.option_names()

+    errors += [_messages.unknown_parameter(key, suggest(key, known))

+               for key in unknown]

+    if errors:

+        raise CliError(_messages.parameter_errors(errors))

+    return bound

+

+

+def _apply_defaults(synopsis, words, options, defaults):

+    words = list(words)

+    names = synopsis.positional_names()

+    for name in names[len(words):]:

+        if name not in defaults:

+            break

+        words.append(defaults[name])

+    for name in synopsis.option_names():

+        if name not in options and name in defaults:

+            options[name] = defaults[name]

+    return words, options

+

+

+def bind(path, synopsis, defaults, words, options):

+    """Validate ``words`` and ``options`` against ``synopsis``.

+

+    ``options`` is a sequence of ``(name, value)`` pairs where ``value`` is a

+    string or ``None`` (no ``=`` given). Raises ``MissingPositional`` when

+    required positionals are absent and ``CliError`` for other problems.

+    """

+    malformed = synopsis.malformed_parts()

+    if malformed:

+        raise CliError(_messages.invalid_synopsis(path, malformed))

+    _check_positionals(synopsis, list(words))

+    bound = _bind_options(synopsis, options)

+    words, bound = _apply_defaults(synopsis, words, bound, dict(defaults))

+    return BoundArguments(words, bound)

+"""Convenience rewrites applied before dispatch.

+

+Secret: which shortcut spellings are rewritten into canonical commands and

+how — currently ``<command> --help`` becomes ``help <command>`` and a bare

+``--version`` becomes ``cli version``.

+"""

+

+from . import tokens as _tokens

+

+

+def _is_bare_flag(token, name):

+    return token.is_option() and token.name == name and token.value is None

+

+

+def _rewrite_version(items):

+    if any(not t.is_option() for t in items):

+        return items

+    if not any(_is_bare_flag(t, "version") for t in items):

+        return items

+    kept = [t for t in items if not _is_bare_flag(t, "version")]

+    return kept + [_tokens.positional("cli"), _tokens.positional("version")]

+

+

+def _rewrite_help(items):

+    if not any(_is_bare_flag(t, "help") for t in items):

+        return items

+    kept = [t for t in items if not _is_bare_flag(t, "help")]

+    help_word = _tokens.positional("help")

+    for index, token in enumerate(kept):

+        if not token.is_option():

+            return kept[:index] + [help_word] + kept[index:]

+    return kept + [help_word]

+

+

+def apply(items):

+    """Return a new token list with all rewrites applied."""

+    return _rewrite_help(_rewrite_version(list(items)))

+"""Pipeline wiring.

+

+Secret: the order in which the stages run (lex, rewrite, extract globals,

+resolve, bind, run) and how failures map to output and exit codes.

+"""

+

+from . import binding, catalog, dispatch, help_text, rewrites, runtime_config, tokens

+from .command_tree import CommandTree

+from .errors import CliError, MissingPositional

+from .output import Output

+

+

+class CommandContext:

+    """Everything a command handler may use."""

+

+    def __init__(self, command, args, out, config, tree):

+        self.command = command

+        self.args = args

+        self.out = out

+        self.config = config

+        self.tree = tree

+

+

+def build_tree():

+    tree = CommandTree()

+    catalog.register_all(tree)

+    return tree

+

+

+def run(argv, env, stdout, stderr, tree=None):

+    """Run one invocation and return its exit code."""

+    out = Output(stdout, stderr)

+    try:

+        items = rewrites.apply(tokens.lex(argv))

+        config, items = runtime_config.extract(items, env)

+    except CliError as exc:

+        out.error(exc.message)

+        return exc.exit_code

+    out = Output(stdout, stderr, quiet=config.quiet(), debug=config.debug())

+    tree = tree if tree is not None else build_tree()

+

+    words = [t.text for t in items if not t.is_option()] or ["help"]

+    options = [(t.name, t.value) for t in items if t.is_option()]

+    node = None

+    try:

+        node, remaining = dispatch.resolve(tree, words)

+        out.debug(f"Resolved command '{node.path}' with arguments {remaining}")

+        if not node.is_runnable():

+            out.usage(help_text.composite_usage(node))

+            return 0

+        bound = binding.bind(node.path, node.synopsis, node.defaults(),

+                             remaining, options)

+        result = node.run(CommandContext(node, bound, out, config, tree))

+        return int(result or 0)

+    except MissingPositional:

+        out.usage(help_text.usage_line(node))

+        return 1

+    except CliError as exc:

+        out.error(exc.message)

+        return exc.exit_code

+"""Output streams.

+

+Secret: which stream each kind of output goes to, the prefix it carries,

+and how quiet and debug modes affect it.

+"""

+

+

+class Output:

+    def __init__(self, stdout, stderr, quiet=False, debug=False):

+        self._stdout = stdout

+        self._stderr = stderr

+        self._quiet = quiet

+        self._debug = debug

+

+    def _write(self, stream, text):

+        stream.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")

+

+    def line(self, text=""):

+        """Command result data; always shown."""

+        self._write(self._stdout, text)

+

+    def usage(self, text):

+        """Help and usage text; always shown."""

+        self._write(self._stdout, text)

+

+    def log(self, text):

+        if not self._quiet:

+            self._write(self._stdout, text)

+

+    def success(self, text):

+        if not self._quiet:

+            self._write(self._stdout, f"Success: {text}")

+

+    def warning(self, text):

+        if not self._quiet:

+            self._write(self._stderr, f"Warning: {text}")

+

+    def error(self, text):

+        self._write(self._stderr, f"Error: {text}")

+

+    def debug(self, text):

+        if self._debug:

+            self._write(self._stderr, f"Debug: {text}")

+"""Help and usage layout.

+

+Secret: how help listings, command help pages and usage lines are laid out:

+section order, column alignment and wording of the surrounding text.

+"""

+

+from .messages import program_name

+

+

+def _columns(nodes):

+    width = max((len(n.name) for n in nodes), default=0)

+    return "\n".join(f"  {n.name.ljust(width)}  {n.description}".rstrip()

+                     for n in nodes)

+

+

+def _invocation(node):

+    """``appctl <path> <synopsis>`` for one command."""

+    words = [program_name(), node.path]

+    if node.has_children() and not node.is_runnable():

+        words.append("<command>")

+    else:

+        words.append(node.synopsis.text())

+    return " ".join(w for w in words if w)

+

+

+def top_level_help(tree):

+    prog = program_name()

+    return (

+        f"usage: {prog} <command> [<subcommand>] [<args>] [--<flags>]\n"

+        "\n"

+        "Available commands:\n"

+        "\n"

+        f"{_columns(tree.root.children())}\n"

+        "\n"

+        f"See '{prog} help <command>' for more information on a specific command."

+    )

+

+

+def usage_line(node):

+    return f"usage: {_invocation(node)}"

+

+

+def composite_usage(node):

+    lines = []

+    for index, child in enumerate(node.children()):

+        lead = "usage:" if index == 0 else "   or:"

+        lines.append(f"{lead} {_invocation(child)}")

+    lines.append("")

+    lines.append(f"See '{program_name()} help {node.path} <command>' "

+                 "for more information on a specific command.")

+    return "\n".join(lines)

+

+

+def command_help(node):

+    sections = [("NAME", f"  {program_name()} {node.path}")]

+    if node.description:

+        sections.append(("DESCRIPTION", f"  {node.description}"))

+    synopses = []

+    if node.is_runnable():

+        synopses.append(" ".join(

+            w for w in (program_name(), node.path, node.synopsis.text()) if w))

+    if node.has_children():

+        synopses.append(f"{program_name()} {node.path} <command>")

+    sections.append(("SYNOPSIS", "\n".join(f"  {s}" for s in synopses)))

+    if node.alias:

+        sections.append(("ALIAS", f"  {node.alias}"))

+    defaults = node.defaults()

+    if defaults:

+        positional = set(node.synopsis.positional_names())

+        sections.append(("DEFAULTS", "\n".join(

+            f"  <{key}>: {value}" if key in positional else f"  --{key}: {value}"

+            for key, value in defaults.items())))

+    if node.has_children():

+        sections.append(("SUBCOMMANDS", _columns(node.children())))

+    return "\n\n".join(f"{title}\n\n{body}" for title, body in sections)
